newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Perez Companc Venezuelan oil production hits high.
newsitem.headline: Perez Companc Venezuelan oil production hits high.

text.p: Argentine oil company Perez Companc's crude production in Venezuela has hit a new high of 38,000 barrels per day, with 50,000 bpd possibly seen for early 1988, company manager Horacio Begaries told Reuters.

"We have an expansion plan that will provide steady if not dramatic growth," Begaries said referring to the Ortiupano-Leona concession in eastern Venezuela that it successfully bid for in 1994 and now operates with Petroleos de Venezuela (PdVSA) affiliate Corpoven.
Production then stood at only 9,000 bpd and may rise to 50,000 bpd by early 1998 "as conditions permit". The field is Perez Companc's largest oil investment in Latin America.
In January of this year Perez Companc also won the concession for the San Carlos field in central Venezuela.

Geological studies and preliminary drilling will be completed in the next six to eight months at a total cost of $14 million. A further $30 million investment is envisaged, Begaries said, with production coming on stream around November of next year.
